function: Joint design of BS active beamforming and STAR-IRS reflection and transmission beamforming to maximize multi-cell energy efficiency under imperfect cascaded CSI (p. 1, 5).
system: Three cells: BS with M = 2-8 antennas, energy-splitting STAR-IRS (N = 10-60 elements), two single-antenna UEs; direct links blocked; frequency not stated (p. 3, 12, 15).
method: Multi-agent DDPG with a GNN per cell, centralized training and decentralized execution; reinforcement learning with robust training on perfect and imperfect CSI (p. 7-10).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rician fading (factor 10), path loss 35.6+22log10(d), Gaussian CSI error model, random UE walk; no standard channel model or measurements (p. 3-4, 8, 12).
test_conditions: Trained over episodes with random UE positions and imperfect CSI; results averaged over 1000 random UE position realizations; network size set per N; no unseen scenario (p. 8, 12-13).
baselines: Learned: MASAC [48]; PDMADRL without GNN (ablation). Non-learned: random beamforming. Variants: symmetric STAR-IRS, conventional IRS, perfect-CSI, non-robust training; AO-SCA only in complexity (p. 11-13).
metrics: System energy efficiency versus transmit power, STAR-IRS elements, BS antennas and rate threshold; average reward per episode; implementation run-time (p. 12-15).
complexity: Training and implementation complexity orders derived (Table I); measured run-time 0.0021-0.0093 s versus 0.0099-0.0191 s for MASAC at N = 10-60 (Table II) (p. 11-12).
q1_support: p. 3: "Rician fading models are assumed for the channels of the BSs-STAR-IRSs and" STAR-IRS-UE links; p. 12: "The path losses are modeled as 35.6 + 22 log 10(dindirect )[dB] [49]"; custom simulator, no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 13: "the average of each simulated outcome is computed over 1000 random UE position realizations"; same distribution as training (random UE walk, p. 8), and the network is sized for each N (p. 12), so no unseen condition is tested.
q3_support: p. 13: "A framework based on a multiagent soft actor-critic algorithm [48] to solve (P1)"; non-learned, p. 12: "A STAR-IRS-aided system with all active and passive beamforming set up randomly while satisfying the constraints"; both compared on energy efficiency in Figs. 5-8 (p. 14-15).
q4_support: p. 11: "Table I compares the implementation complexity of the conventional prior methods" with the proposed approach; p. 12: "we assess the implementation time of adopting the proposed GNN-enhanced PDMADRL algorithm in comparison to the MASAC-based algorithm"
q5_support: p. 16: "Both perfect and imperfect artificially generated CSI were used to evaluate the performance functions"; synthetic channels, no code or data link and no public dataset anywhere in the paper.
notes: Area 3: the learned DDPG agents set the BS precoders and the STAR-IRS coefficients. q3 rests on the random scheme (non-learned) and MASAC [48] (learned); PDMADRL without GNN is an ablation and the perfect-CSI and non-robust designs are training variants, so they do not count; AO-SCA appears only in the complexity table (p. 11). Frequency band and the CSI error level are not given in Table III (p. 12).
